issues.where: Spear.lean lem_add_BTZ_param / lem_add_BTZ_param_line(_e0) (conclusion `ContinuousOn τS`); REPORT.json lem:add_BTZ_param hypotheses[2], findings[2]
issues.problem: The weakening is disclosed, the row is partial, and earlier audits (WP-41i rounds 2–3) accepted it, so this is not a new defect. It is recorded so the master session can decide it. B21 defines a Cauchy surface topologically (BTZ_1.tex:222: 'a topological hypersurface Σ which intersects exactly once every inextendible causal curve'). Read literally, Lemma 2.4 ('smooth positive function τ_Σ') is false for a non-smooth topological Σ, e.g. a Lipschitz acausal graph with a corner over the axis. DEC-27 would then ask for a counterexample next to the strongest true form. The file proves the C⁰ form for topological Σ and has neither (a) a counterexample to smoothness, nor (b) a C¹ form under a C¹ spacelike Σ. B21 l.673 ('a given spacelike Cauchy surface') reads Σ as spacelike, and form (b) is the one that reading calls for. For gx, DEC-107 puts the C¹ trace on the shaft circle into IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy itself, so nothing downstream needs (b).
issues.fix: Either add a finding that names the paper's literal statement false for topological Σ (with a one-line counterexample) and frames the C⁰ form as its strongest true form, or ask the author for a ruling that accepts the C⁰ reading under DEC-107. No Lean change is required for gx.

issues.where: Spear.lean frontier_spear / interior_spear (model only); REPORT.json Def 2.1 hypotheses[0]
issues.problem: Def 2.1 asserts 'The boundary of U is the union of the head and the shaft', with U ⊆ M. The file proves this only in the model (frontier_spear: ∂ spear = head ∪ shaft in 𝔼₀). ψ is an open embedding on W ⊇ spear, so ψ(head ∪ shaft) ⊆ ∂_M U follows. The reverse inclusion needs U = ψ(spear) to be closed in M, i.e. no sequence going up the unbounded spear converges in M outside U. That is neither proved nor discussed. The REPORT does say 'proved in the model' and the row is partial, so nothing is overclaimed; the M-level part of the assertion is simply missing.
issues.fix: Add one sentence to Def 2.1's findings or hypotheses saying the boundary claim is certified in the model only, and whether the M-level claim is expected to need GH (closedness of ψ(spear)). Optionally prove it for GH M from IsFullFutureBTZRay.not_tendsto-type escape arguments.

checked_clean: (1) Builds: lake env lean is clean, the real sorry count is 0, matching REPORT.json, and the module is up to date with nothing upstream rebuilt.

(2) lem:tube statement (lem_tube_e0): GH + IsE0CauchyMaximal + p ∈ S0 M ⊢ ∃ R U, IsSpearNbhd p R U, with no further hypothesis; hLine/hSC are discharged by the strict E0LM lemmas. IsE0CauchyMaximal quantifies over T2, connected, second countable 𝔼₀-targets N. Restricting the class of N makes the hypothesis WEAKER, which is correct for kb/0011, and isE0CauchyMaximal_iff_isETTMaximal proves it equal to Dev.IsETTMaximal (DEC-77(c)). The only strengthening is M ranging over 𝔼₀ rather than 𝔼_{≥0}, tagged correctly as 'strengthened' and kept partial.

(2) No circularity in Lemma 2.3: exists_spearDevelopment builds the SpearDevelopment unconditionally from GH and a BTZ point. CylChartData is satisfiable (exists_cylChartData), and its `convex` field is B21's l.647 normalisation, proved from strong causality rather than assumed. The Cauchy embedding M₀ → M₂ uses the now-proved globallyHyperbolic_glued and isCauchySurface_glued, so the GH of M₂ that B21 never argues is carried by a proof (DEC-108).

(2) DEC-108 (1): globallyHyperbolic_glued is the strict library's full (CE Glued).GloballyHyperbolic. Causality and the unmixed diamonds come via Causal.Causality.TwoPiece; the mixed diamonds come from CylChartData.isCompact_diamond_mixed (the union of two continuous images of compacts), not from TwoPiece.isCompact_diamond_mixed, which needs a common Cauchy surface. That is as the dispatch prescribed.

(2) DEC-108 (2): isCauchySurface_glued concludes that ι false '' S is a Cauchy surface of M₂. The only added instance, [SecondCountableTopology M], is a DEC-66 convention carried by the only caller; it is reported and is not a statement change of any paper row.

(2) DEC-108 (3): lem_add_BTZ_param_line(_e0) takes the paper's hypothesis literally: a spear neighbourhood of an arbitrary vertex q, and p ∈ connectedComponentIn (S0 M) q ∩ I⁻(Σ). Both cases are proved. The future case uses exists_spearNbhd_below (continuation by the infimum of good parameters) and CylChartData.exists_spear_below (normalisation on the connected component of the overlap by rigidity, injectivity from causal convexity of the chart cylinder). The paper's l.725 typo ('q in the future of q') is reported.

(2) Lemma 2.4's conclusion encodes 'Σ ∩ S is the graph of τ_Σ over the closed disc, in the shaft' exactly: ∀ x ∈ spear v R', ψ(x) ∈ Σ ↔ x.1 = τS x.2, with τS > v + R'/2 on ‖z‖ ≤ R'. That makes each (τS z, z) a spear point. Read through B21's normalisation Φ(p) = (−R/2,0,0), 'positive' and 'in the shaft' are the same condition τ > v + R/2 (the shaft starts at τ = 0 there), so the reading is consistent with the paper's own proof.

(2) Def 2.1: IsSpearNbhd (ψ = φ⁻¹, an injective 𝔼₀-morphism on an open W ⊇ spear, vertex ↦ p, U = ψ(spear)) is non-trivial, witnessed by isSpearNbhd_model, and spear = J⁺(vertex) ∩ {r ≤ R} is proved (spear_eq_Jplus_inter), matching V := J⁺(φ(p)) ∩ {r ≤ R}. The head/shaft finding was re-derived from B21's own proof: its curves c(s) = ((s−R)/2, s, θ) put the future cone of an axis point at τ − r/2 = const, so with vertex −2R the head is r = 2(τ + 2R) and the rim sits at τ = −3R/2, not r = 2(τ − R) and τ ≥ 0. The finding is correct. 'Neighbourhood of ]p,+∞[' is proved (IsSpearNbhd.exists_ray_mem_nhds together with IsFullFutureBTZRay.exists_eq_of_line).

(2) Full future BTZ rays: exists_fullFutureBTZRay_e0 takes the DEC-77(c)-corrected hypotheses (GH + Cauchy-maximal; Cauchy-completeness not needed). The IsFullFutureBTZRay reading is shown to have the expected properties: in sing₀, injective, continuous, future-directed, without a future limit, covering the future half of its line. The citation correction 'Lemma 2.4 → Lemma 2.3' (RamcovGX.tex:2352) is right: Lemma 2.4 presupposes a spear neighbourhood.
